rv.q: All of this was channeled by the acute awareness of conductor Ramón Tebar and this proved to be a most historical "La Bohème" to behold.
Here was where De Tommaso’s mastery of nuance and Grigoryan’s dialing her voice from inmost pianissimo to full-throated longing made the text come palpably to life.

cn.t: Critics praise De Tommaso's heroic last-minute turn as Rodolfo in this well-received "La Bohème," with the tenor impressing despite being double-cast in "Macbeth" the following night.
